title: feat(plugin-list): a page list-view node is written data / type, and the metadata page reads properties.type as the list kind (objectui#12099)
body:
Fixes #12099
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Ruling: objectstack-ai/objectstack#22444, comment `6100463199` (ruling C). Claim: comment `6213954533` on objectui#12099. Written by the dispatched os-dev of the `domain:ui` seat 3, session `session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4`.

## What changes

- **Registration** (`packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx`). `list-view` and its `view:list` alias (one renderer, so one spelling) publish `data` (object: the spec's `ViewData`, `{ provider: 'object', object }` names the object) and `type` (enum: the nine kinds a list view draws) in place of `objectName` and `viewType`. Neither is required: a `dataSource` binding can name the object. `list-view`'s `defaultProps` are `{ data: { provider: 'object', object: '' }, columns: [], filter: [], sort: [], options: {} }`. There is no `type` default: an absent kind is already the grid (the spec's list view `type` defaults to `grid`), absence lets a bound saved view's kind apply, and a `type` there would read as the registry key to anything that spreads the defaults onto a node.
- **How the kind travels** (`ListViewBlock`). `SchemaRenderer`'s hoist copies a node's `properties` onto the node, never copies the bag's `type` (the node's own `type` is the registry key), and keeps the bag on the node. So the `list-view` renderer reads `properties.type` itself and hands it to `ListView` as `viewType`, before the element-data-source gate, so a kind the node states outranks a bound saved view's kind. A value that names no kind a list view draws is dropped, and the list is a grid. `HOIST_PROTECTED_KEYS` is unchanged (hypothesis 2 below).
- **No fallback read.** `ListViewBlock` removes a page node's own `objectName` and `viewType`, flat or hoisted from the bag, before the gate and `ListView` see the node. Each logs one console warning per process naming what to write instead. A node that names its object only as `objectName` therefore names none, and draws the "no object named" hint, which now names `data.object`. `ListViewBlock` draws that hint after the binding is applied; the gate's own `requiresObject` hint names the gate's object key, which is `objectName`.
- **The object.** `data` passes through as authored. `normalizeListViewSchema`'s existing `object`-provider fold (objectui#7477) lands it on `ListView`'s `objectName`. A bound `dataSource.object` still lands on `objectName` through the gate and outranks `data.object`. `objectName` and `viewType` remain the hand-off keys between the gate and the `ListView` component; neither is read off the page node.
- **Docs.** plugin-list README: a new section "On a page — `data` and `type`", and the page-binding section now names `data`. `content/docs/guide/data-source.md`: `list-view`'s object key is `data` and its hint names `data.object`.
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/12099-list-view-page-spelling.md`, `@object-ui/plugin-list` minor, with the breaking part for page nodes in the old spelling spelled out.

## The PM's mechanism hypotheses, measured

1. **Holds** at `8614705`: the registration's inputs carried the shared `objectName` input and a `viewType` enum, its `defaultProps` `objectName: ''` and `viewType: 'grid'`, and `SchemaRenderer` declared `HOIST_PROTECTED_KEYS = new Set(['type', 'id'])`. A scratch probe (deleted) through the real `SchemaRenderer` and the real registration, with view spies: `{ type: 'list-view', properties: { data: { provider: 'object', object: X }, type: 'kanban', kanban } }` drew a **grid** over X (the `data` half already bound; only the kind was lost), and the flat old spelling drew a kanban.
2. **Holds.** The hoist keeps `properties` on the node after copying it, so the renderer can read `properties.type` itself. A global change would reach the two spec `ComponentPropsMap` rows that declare a `type` member, `page:tabs` (the tab style) and `element:metadata_viewer` (2 of 59 rows, read from the installed `@objectstack/spec` 18.0.0-next.1). Chosen: the narrow read in `ListViewBlock`.
3. **Partly holds.** On the page path the object already resolved from `data` (the fold above) and from `dataSource.object` (the gate). What moved: the node's `objectName` is not read, and the hint judges `data` (an `object` provider counts only with a non-empty `object`; rows and any other provider count as a source). The gate still lands a binding on `objectName`, as the internal hand-off: landing it "into `data`" would either overwrite an authored rows or `value`-provider `data` or need a new gate option in `@object-ui/react`, outside this claim. ⚠️ The `objectui validate` record-source rule did **not** move: it lives in `@object-ui/types` (the `list-view` arm's `requireRecordSource` call). See the stop below.
4. **Holds, with the stop it predicts.** The page path and the React component props are one type: `ListViewBlock` is a `forwardRef` over `ListViewProps`, whose `schema` is `@object-ui/types`' `ListViewSchema`, the zod-derived face that `objectui validate` and `StrictAnyComponentSchema` judge a `list-view` node with (`type` is the `'list-view'` discriminator literal; `objectName` and `viewType` are its members; it has no `properties` member). Measured on that face at `8614705`: the ruled page node is refused (strict: `unrecognized_keys` `properties`, plus `RECORD_SOURCE_REQUIRED` at `objectName`; tolerant: the record-source issue), a flat `data`-only node is refused the same way, and the flat old spelling is accepted. Separating the two needs a `@object-ui/types` change, a contract face, so it is not in this PR (open question below).
5. **Census** below.
6. **Cross-repo consumers** below.

## Census: nodes written with `objectName` / `viewType` (hypothesis 5)

Instrument: a node-literal scan over `git ls-files` (a `list-view` or `view:list` type literal in TS or JSON, or the html tag) with `objectName` / `viewType` within the next 8 lines. Positive control: the first `ListView` example in `packages/plugin-list/README.md` (hit). The ruling's count of about 7 files and 45 mentions is its own reading. Non-test result at `8614705`, 5 files and 12 sites:

- `packages/plugin-list/README.md`, 8 sites: each one an example of the `ListView` React component's `schema` prop, not a page node.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectDataPage.tsx`: each renders the `ListView` component directly with the schema it builds, not through `SchemaRenderer` and the registration.
- `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`: the schema handed to a host's `renderListView`; the console's host (app-shell `ObjectView`) renders the `ListView` component with it.
- `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`: one doc comment.

So no objectui source, README or guide writes `objectName` / `viewType` on a node that reaches the `list-view` registration, and no runtime-built node in this repository reaches it. The four component-prop sites stay as they are: on that type `type` is the discriminator, so the kind cannot be spelled `type` there without the `@object-ui/types` change. The page-path test fixtures that bound a list through the old spelling were respelled (Tests).

## Stopped, not shipped: the `@object-ui/types` face

`objectui validate` (both faces) and this repository's own `check:doc-json` gate still judge a `list-view` node in the spelling before this PR: they accept a flat `objectName` / `viewType` node that the renderer no longer reads, and refuse the ruled page spelling, telling the author to declare `objectName`. The README's new page example therefore carries a `doc-json: fragment` declaration naming this; the gate re-judges it on every run, so it turns red (stale) the day the face accepts the page spelling. The decision request is in the os-dev report on the card.

## Contract evidence (Clause-②)

- **The `Clause-②:` line**: corrected by the dispatching seat from `yes (widening, with the old spelling retired)` to `yes (narrowing)`, per the contract review of record `6216255338` (its ②). The diff widens and narrows; the closed pair takes one arm, and the narrowing arm is the one that decides the review owed (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`). Nothing in the tree moved.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-list` built `dist`**, measured: built once with the `8614705` versions of `src/index.tsx` and `src/ListViewBlock.tsx` and once at this head. All 10 `dist/*.d.ts` files are byte-identical. The runtime contract moved in `dist/index.js`: `list-view`'s inputs `objectName` and `viewType` became `data` and `type` (the same on `view:list`), and its `defaultProps` `{ objectName: '', viewType: 'grid', … }` became `{ data: { provider: 'object', object: '' }, … }`.
- **`@object-ui/react`**: no file under `packages/react` or `packages/types` changed (an empty `git diff 8614705` over both), so neither built output moves.
- **Widens**: a page `list-view` reads `properties.type` as its kind, and the published inputs gain `data` and `type`. **Narrows**: a page node's `objectName` and `viewType` are no longer read, and the published manifest no longer lists them, so an html-tier `objectName` or `viewType` attribute now draws `unknown-prop`.

## Cross-repo consumers (named, not changed here)

- **HotCRM**: its home page builds embedded list views with `properties: { objectName, viewType: 'grid', … }` (hotcrm `src/sales/pages/home.page.ts`, per triage `6101018189`). Under this PR alone those lists draw the "no object named" hint.
- **objectstack**: `sdui.manifest.json` lists renderer inputs; the console build's manifest now lists `data` and `type` for `list-view` and `view:list`.
- **For the cloud seat**, verbatim from triage `6213876820`:

  > cloud moves `.objectui-sha` past this card only with an `.objectstack-sha` that carries #22444's conversion

  (There `#22444` is objectstack-ai/objectstack#22444: the ADR-0087 conversion of stored page nodes, `objectName` to `data` and `viewType` to `type`, that lands with the console pin move.)

## Tests

- New pin `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListViewBlock.pageCarrierSpelling-12099.test.tsx`, through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registration: the card's kanban through `properties.type` (bound to the object `properties.data` names, queried, and the `object-kanban` node is the one `ListView` builds, so the node dispatched as `list-view`); a grid when `properties.type` is absent or names no kind; the same on `view:list`; ⛔ no read of `objectName` / `viewType` in the bag or flat (hint naming `data.object`, no query); a `viewType` beside a working `data` changes nothing; one warning per retired key per process; `properties.type` beside a `dataSource` binding, outranking a bound saved view's kind, with the view's kind applying when absent; the registrations' inputs and `defaultProps`.
- Fixtures respelled (each used the old spelling only to bind the list; none pinned the old branch except where noted): plugin-list `ListView.sharedGate` (the authored-kind case now authors `properties.type`), `ListView.elementDataSource`, `ListView.invalidationRefetch-10572`, `ObjectGallery.filterContextTokens-10666`, `htmlTierColumnSpellings-6598` (form 8a now expects the hint to name `data.object`), `htmlTierListViewDefaultColumns-6598`; console `filterContextTokensSweep-10666`, `htmlTierDataSourceInputDeclaration-6678`, `objectname-neither-hint-11605` (list rows name their object in `data`, and a new row pins that the retired `objectName` draws the hint), `objectname-binding-required-11605` (the object key read off the binding doc, plus a row pinning `unknown-prop` for the retired attributes), `public-block-binding-reach` (`list-view` left the population of blocks that declare `objectName`, with the reason).
- Union run at the final head: at `9e4c5ee`, `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over the whole `packages/plugin-list/` plus 71 named files elsewhere that render a `list-view` through the registry or read its published inputs (console manifest and html-tier pins, app-shell list surfaces, plugin-view, react, components, sdui-parser, types): `Test Files  212 passed (212)` / `Tests  2904 passed (2904)` (lock verdict `command-exit 0`). `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list type-check` (both projects; the test project includes the new pin) exits 0 after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-list^...' build`.
- Ablations, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` with the restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`, direction predicted before running:
  - drop the `properties.type` hand-off: predicted and observed 5 red (the kanban case, `view:list`, both binding cases, the sharedGate authored-kind case), 30 green.
  - keep the retired keys on the hand-off: predicted and observed 4 red (both `objectName`-only hint cases, the `viewType`-beside-`data` case, the warning case), 14 green.

## Gates

Local subset, each exit code captured before any pipe, at `9e4c5ee`:

- 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `check:i18n-keys` (the hint's inline default equals the `en` pack), `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-json` (the README page example sits in the `declared` bucket, re-judged as refused by the face), `check:doc-fences`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:prompt-keys`, `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:spec-symbols`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`; `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 14 changed TS files: 0 errors (the warnings are the existing `any` patterns of the respelled files; the new pin carries none).
- `scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 17 changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI: `check:doc-snippets` (exit 2, precondition: 34 packages unbuilt; no ts fence changed), `check:sdui-registration-pins` (exit 2, needs a console build), `check:readme-exports` (exit 1 on 382 self-imports it could not judge, all in packages outside this build closure; plugin-list's README drew none, and the judged set has `0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated`), the console `type-check` (its closure is the whole workspace; only test literals changed there), `pnpm lint` and the full test farm.

## Acceptance notes

- **The html tier has no attribute for the kind.** Its parser refuses a `type` attribute by design (the tag is the component), so an html-tier list-view tag cannot state a kind; a bound saved view's kind still applies. The `type` input is published and reachable on metadata pages and on the react tier (whose `type` attribute is parked as `specType`, unchanged).
- **`check:doc-types` reads `properties.type` as a node type**: every `type` literal in a code block is judged against the registry, so a page example with `"type": "kanban"` in `properties` is flagged. The README states the kind in prose beside the example instead. Noted, not filed.
- **React tier, read from source, not run**: `ListView` with `type="kanban"` and a `dataSource` naming a saved view parks the kind as `specType`, which `normalizeListViewSchema` reads only when `viewType` is absent, and the gate writes the view's kind to `viewType` first; so there the saved view's kind would win over the author's. Not changed here (the react tier's carrier), not filed (not reproduced).
